title: Bound semantic portfolio diagnosis to prioritized scores
description:
As an optimization operator, I want semantic diagnosis limited to the declared priority scope with explicit coverage and fail-closed approval behavior, so that a periodic portfolio run is predictable, affordable, and cannot approve undiagnosed targets.

Included:
- Assess every ranked score deterministically.
- Diagnose the ranked top ten plus every monitoring candidate.
- Deduplicate the selected union in original rank order.
- Require completed diagnosis before approval readiness.
- Report selected, completed, skipped, and failed diagnosis coverage.
- Enforce an explicit nested semantic-work limit or fail before model calls.

Excluded:
- Optimizer launch, score changes, champion changes, or feedback-setting changes.
- Client-specific ranking or policy.

Feature: Bounded semantic portfolio diagnosis

Scenario: Diagnose the declared priority union
  Given an exact ranked portfolio and completed assessments
  When the portfolio run enters semantic diagnosis
  Then it diagnoses only the top ten ranked opportunities and all monitoring candidates
  And overlapping targets are diagnosed once in rank order

Scenario: Keep undiagnosed targets out of approval
  Given a score assessed as ready but outside the semantic diagnosis scope
  When approval targets are prepared
  Then the score is not approval-ready
  And its missing diagnosis is reported explicitly

Scenario: Publish honest diagnosis coverage
  Given a bounded semantic diagnosis selection
  When a milestone is published
  Then the evidence reports selected, completed, skipped, and failed counts
  And it never labels semantic portfolio coverage as exhaustive

Scenario: Fail closed on exhausted semantic budget
  Given the configured semantic-work limit would be exceeded
  When diagnosis would invoke another model-backed check
  Then no additional model call is made
  And the run records an incomplete diagnosis blocker.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Dogfood reproduction confirmed that deterministic assessment completed account-wide, while semantic diagnosis iterated beyond the declared priority scope and lacked an effective nested model-work budget. The run was interrupted before approval or mutation. Next: add outside-in failing coverage for bounded selection, fail-closed readiness, coverage evidence, and semantic limits; then implement the smallest fix and rerun the safe read-only workflow.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Living-report presentation now identifies the current activity, next durable checkpoint, inspected/ranked/unranked counts, cooldown exclusions, assessment progress, bounded diagnosis progress, and pending approvals. Approval evidence is published before structured HITL can suspend. Focused report and portfolio suite: 39 passed; runtime validation is next.
